claims.text: Structurally modified transition metal dichalcogenides will exhibit enhanced HER catalytic activity compared with traditional platinum-based catalysts.
Structurally modified transition metal dichalcogenides will exhibit enhanced HOR catalytic activity compared with traditional platinum-based catalysts.
Structurally modified transition metal dichalcogenides will be more durable than platinum-based catalysts during HER and HOR.
Doping or structural engineering can optimize the electronic properties of TMDs.
The layered structure of TMDs provides increased catalytic surface area.
The layered structure of TMDs provides an increased number of catalytically active sites.
Modified electronic properties of TMDs improve charge transfer during HER and HOR.
Modified electronic properties of TMDs lower the energy barriers of HER and HOR pathways.
Improved charge transfer and lower reaction barriers enhance catalytic activity.
Modified TMDs will have a higher turnover frequency for HER and HOR than platinum-based catalysts.
Modified TMDs will have a lower HER and HOR overpotential than platinum-based catalysts.
The higher turnover frequency and lower overpotential of modified TMDs will improve catalytic efficiency.
The higher turnover frequency and lower overpotential of modified TMDs will improve durability.
Traditional platinum-based catalysts have known HER and HOR performance metrics suitable for use as a baseline.
The proposed performance improvement applies only to structurally modified TMDs and not to pristine TMDs.
The magnitude of performance improvement may depend on the specific TMD and modification method.
